problem: Learning accurate nonlinear dynamical models from limited data while ensuring they are suitable for downstream control design remains challenging.
approach: Enforces controllability as a structural property during Koopman representation learning in latent space, where the system admits linear dynamics, using a canonical parameterization and Gramian-based regularization implemented as a Neural ODE framework.
contribution: Proves controllability of learned latent models implies controllability in nominal state space, enabling data-efficient learning of models suitable for model predictive control.

problem: Text-driven image editing with existing approaches struggles to balance structural preservation with flexible modifications or requires costly fine-tuning.
approach: W-Edit decomposes diffusion features via wavelet transforms into multi-scale frequency bands to disentangle structural anchors from editable details, using lightweight replacement and inversion-based frequency modulation.
contribution: Achieves high-quality text-driven image editing across diverse scenarios, outperforming previous training-free approaches through frequency-based modulation.

problem: Off-policy reinforcement learning for LLMs suffers from sharp policy entropy decline, unstable optimization, and gradient explosions when training on stale data.
approach: BAPO identifies optimization imbalance and fixed clipping flaws, proposing dynamic clipping bounds that adaptively re-balance positive and negative contributions while preserving entropy.
contribution: Achieves stable, data-efficient off-policy RL training; a 7B BAPO model surpasses SkyWork-OR1-7B and a 32B model matches o3-mini and Gemini-2.5-Flash-Thinking on AIME benchmarks.

problem: Spiking Transformers face a substantial performance gap versus ANNs and considerable memory overhead due to unfocused global attention and large attention matrix storage.
approach: LRF-Dyn integrates localized receptive fields into spiking self-attention and approximates charge-fire-reset dynamics of spiking neurons, reducing memory requirements during inference.
contribution: Lowers memory overhead while delivering significant performance improvements for energy-efficient vision Transformers.

problem: Capturing complex two-way fluid-solid interactions remains challenging because existing deep learning methods are limited to simplified one-way scenarios or struggle with dynamic heterogeneous interactions.
approach: Fisale uses Arbitrary Lagrangian-Eulerian inspiration with multiscale latent grids to model the coupling interface explicitly, applying partitioned coupling decomposition for progressive nonlinear modeling.
contribution: Flexibly handles complex two-way FSI dynamics on unified representation, excelling in 2D, 3D, and multiple challenging FSI scenarios.

problem: LLM agents fail to learn from accumulated experience in persistent roles, repeatedly making past errors and losing valuable insights.
approach: ReasoningBank stores generalizable reasoning strategies from both successful and failed experiences; memory-aware test-time scaling (MaTTS) synergizes memory with scaled exploration.
contribution: Consistently outperforms existing memory mechanisms on web browsing and software engineering tasks, enabling agents to self-evolve and exhibit emergent behaviors.

problem: Existing test-time adaptation methods for vision-language models are designed for balanced datasets but fail under long-tailed distributions where minor classes are dominated.
approach: L-TTA introduces synergistic prototypes for tail enrichment, learnable rebalancing shortcuts with class re-allocation loss, and balanced entropy minimization with theoretical justification.
contribution: Superior performance across 15 datasets under various long-tailed settings in both accuracy and class balancing.

problem: Existing domain generalization methods use coarse-grained partitioning of stable versus unstable parameters, misclassifying unstable parameters and degrading feature processing.
approach: LDT conducts fine-grained layer-wise partitioning guided by parameter instability levels and introduces dynamic parameter update strategy adapting layer-specific coefficients by gradient variations.
contribution: Demonstrates superior generalization capability across diverse tasks (super-resolution, classification, segmentation) and architectures (Transformer, Mamba, CNN).

problem: Current multimodal benchmarks contain shortcut questions solvable using single modality, yielding unreliable model rankings and inflating benchmark size.
approach: M3-IRT extends classical IRT by decomposing model ability and item difficulty into image-only, text-only, and cross-modal components, estimating genuine cross-modal reasoning.
contribution: Identifies cross-modal questions over shortcuts, preserves ranking fidelity with 50% artificially generated low-quality items, reducing evaluation cost while improving reliability.

problem: Continual representation learning with frozen pretrained models suffers from multicollinearity in similarity-matching and requires computationally prohibitive advanced methods for real-time applications.
approach: Fly-CL adopts bio-inspired design from fly olfactory circuits, progressively resolving multicollinearity through decorrelation with low time complexity.
contribution: Substantially reduces training time while achieving performance comparable to or exceeding state-of-the-art methods with theoretical justification.

problem: LLM ranking systems based on Bradley-Terry models are potentially sensitive to small perturbations in preference data, affecting the reliability of top model rankings.
approach: Proposes a computationally fast method to evaluate robustness by identifying worst-case very small fractions of preference data whose removal most affects rankings.
contribution: Demonstrates rankings of top models can be remarkably sensitive; dropping just 0.003% of human preferences can change Chatbot Arena's top-ranked model.

problem: Current LLM safety evaluations test only what a model can do without assessing what it would do if equipped with high-risk capabilities, missing latent propensity to misuse.
approach: PropensityBench simulates dangerous capabilities via proxy tools in controlled agentic environments with varying operational pressures across 5,874 scenarios and four high-risk domains.
contribution: Uncovers alarming propensity signs: models frequently choose high-risk tools under pressure despite lacking actual execution capability.

problem: Molecular dynamics simulations require expensive fine-grained integration over long biomolecular timescales, limiting their applicability.
approach: MarS-FM learns to sample transitions across discrete Markov State Model states via flow matching, offering two orders of magnitude speedup over MD simulations.
contribution: Outperforms existing generative MD methods on reproducing structural observables (RMSD, radius of gyration, secondary structure) across diverse protein domains.

problem: Transition Matching represents a new generative paradigm but requires systematic investigation of design choices in its head module architecture and sampling strategy.
approach: Conducts large-scale systematic investigation of TM design through 56 different 1.7B text-to-image models and 549 unique evaluations, examining head architecture, training, and sampling.
contribution: Identifies MLP head with specific time weighting and high-frequency sampling as best overall, achieving state-of-the-art among tested baselines with detailed efficiency-quality tradeoffs.

problem: Understanding how graph models generalize to new unseen graphs is limited by existing approaches confined to transductive single-graph settings.
approach: GraphUniverse generates entire families of graphs with persistent semantic communities enabling systematic inductive generalization evaluation with fine-grained control over structural properties.
contribution: Reveals strong transductive performance poorly predicts inductive generalization and robustness to distribution shift depends heavily on model architecture and graph regime.

problem: Existing battery datasets have insufficient scale, coarse-grained labels, and lack real-world operating condition coverage, restricting development of fault diagnosis algorithms.
approach: CH-BatteryGen integrates real on-board operation data with mechanism-constrained generative modeling, covering NCM and LFP batteries with four fault labels and three severity levels.
contribution: Provides large-scale real-world EV battery fault diagnosis dataset supporting classification and grading tasks with baseline results from RF, SVM, LSTM, and CNN models.

problem: Existing LLM-based decompilers struggle to effectively present program source-level structure with original identifiers from binary code.
approach: SK2Decompile uses two-phase decompilation: first recovering semantic structure via intermediate representation with RL for syntactic compliance, then generating meaningful identifiers via RL for semantic similarity.
contribution: Achieves 21.6% re-executability gain over GPT-4-mini on HumanEval and 29.4% R2I improvement over Idioms on GitHub2025.

problem: Learning with noisy labels for high-predictive-accuracy and reliable-confidence requires addressing sample ambiguity and avoiding normality pollution from highly noisy datasets.
approach: TrainRef uses extrinsic reference samples and curates labels into class distributions rather than categorical classes, with reference augmentation and model-dataset co-evolution techniques.
contribution: Uniformly addresses accuracy and confidence calibration, selecting clean samples effectively even with one reference sample per class.

problem: LVLMs' performance on ultrasound imaging remains largely unexplored despite ultrasound's critical role in healthcare and varying interpretation challenges.
approach: U2-BENCH provides comprehensive benchmark evaluating LVLMs on ultrasound understanding across classification, detection, regression, and text generation tasks with 8 clinically inspired tasks.
contribution: Evaluates 23 LVLMs revealing strong image-level classification but persistent challenges in spatial reasoning and clinical language generation.

problem: Open-vocabulary detectors have high confident false positive rates on images without target objects, a flaw masked by standard benchmarks that rarely contain such images.
approach: Identifies vision-language fusion layers in early-fusion OVD architectures as root cause and proposes training-free attention sink tokens appended to input prompts.
contribution: Dramatically reduces background false positives, improving AP on LVIS by more than 5x at false positive rate 0.01 for some models.

problem: VLM multi-view spatial reasoning for robotic manipulation remains underexplored despite multi-camera setups being standard on robotic platforms.
approach: MV-RoboBench evaluates multi-view spatial reasoning across eight subtasks combining spatial understanding and robotic execution with 1.7k manually curated QA items.
contribution: Reveals state-of-the-art models fall far below human performance and strong single-view benchmarks poorly predict multi-view robotic performance.

problem: Long-tailed recognition faces entangled problems at representation, policy, and optimization levels, causing expert homogeneity collapse and unstable meta-learning in multi-expert architectures.
approach: GUIDE systematically disentangles issues at three levels: representation through competitive specialization, policy through uncertainty decomposition, and optimization through two-timescale updates.
contribution: Establishes new state-of-the-art on five challenging LTR benchmarks including ImageNet-LT and iNaturalist 2018.

problem: Practical effectiveness of differential privacy on LLM adaptation remains unclear due to pretraining overlaps with adaptation data potentially undermining DP privacy guarantees.
approach: Systematically varies adaptation data distribution from exact overlaps to out-of-distribution using state-of-the-art attacks (membership inference, canary extraction) across different adaptation methods.
contribution: Shows distribution shifts strongly influence practical privacy risk; LoRA achieves highest empirical protection for OOD data despite identical theoretical guarantees.

problem: Ambivalence/hesitancy recognition in videos for behavioral change analysis lacks existing datasets and baseline methods.
approach: BAH dataset provides 1,118 videos from 224 subjects with frame- and video-level annotations, cues across modalities (face, audio, body, language), and initial baselines for single and multimodal setups.
contribution: Introduces first dataset for ambivalence/hesitancy recognition with comprehensive annotations and demonstrates feasibility through multimodal baseline experiments.

problem: Quantization methods fail to generalize to autoregressive visual generation models due to channel-wise outliers, dynamic token-wise activations, and distribution mismatches.
approach: PTQ4ARVG proposes gain-projected scaling for channel-wise outliers, static token-wise quantization leveraging fixed token length, and distribution-guided calibration for sample-wise mismatches.
contribution: Effectively quantizes ARVG models to 8-bit and 6-bit while maintaining competitive performance without training.

problem: Unified frameworks combining connectivity sparse training and low-rank factorization for LLM pre-training are lacking despite both approaches offering parameter efficiency benefits.
approach: CHTsL integrates dynamic sparse training with low-rank training using an alignment loss to mitigate disagreement between branches and promote collaboration.
contribution: Demonstrates effective integration on LLaMA60M and LLaMA130M, validating the parameter-efficient training approach.

problem: Transferring aligned human-valued behaviors to models fine-tuned on different tasks or distributions is challenging as aligned behavior is forgotten during fine-tuning.
approach: BIRD matches student internal representation structure to teacher via behavior-preserving distillation, outperforming fine-tuning and transfer learning approaches.
contribution: Improves robust accuracy by up to 18%, works with smaller teachers, and explains 85% of transfer success variance through three interpretable representation properties.

problem: Behavioral foundation models rely heavily on complex representation learning objectives that are sensitive to environment coverage, yet their necessity for zero-shot RL is unclear.
approach: RLDP revisits self-supervised next-state prediction with regularization maintaining feature diversity, showing it matches complex objectives while succeeding in low-coverage scenarios.
contribution: Simple regularized latent dynamics prediction serves as strong baseline for behavioral foundation models with improved low-coverage performance.

problem: Memorization in deep neural networks is expensive to compute at scale because rigorous measurement requires training models both with and without the target data point.
approach: Introduces cumulative sample gradient (CSG), the gradient accumulated over training, as computationally efficient memorization proxy showing characteristic rise-peak-decline trajectory.
contribution: CSG achieves five orders of magnitude efficiency gain over exact memorization scores and enables early stopping at weight norm peak without validation set.

problem: Low-rank adaptation methods like LoRA are limited by their factorization structure; exploring alternatives for parameter-efficient fine-tuning remains valuable.
approach: MoSA replaces low-rank factorization with randomized fine-grained weight sharing via broadcasting scalars over fixed tessellation, requiring no architectural changes.
contribution: Matches or surpasses LoRA under strictly matched budgets with analysis showing non-local sharing acts as effective regularizer.

problem: RL with verifiable rewards trains on flawed-positive rollouts containing answer-guessing and jump-in-reasoning that are rewarded equally to fully correct ones.
approach: FAPO introduces parameter-free reward penalty for flawed-positive rollouts and GenRM with process-level rewards for precise error localization.
contribution: Improves outcome correctness, process reliability, and training stability across broad domains without increasing token budget.

problem: Deep learning for material property prediction fails to address inherent diversity and disparity across material tasks through standard pre-training paradigms.
approach: MoMa trains specialized modules across diverse tasks then adaptively composes synergistic modules for each downstream scenario.
contribution: Achieves 14% average improvement over strongest baseline across 17 datasets with strong performance in few-shot and scaling experiments.

problem: Learning from demonstration in continuous control suffers exponential compounding errors with task horizon, limiting practical imitation learning effectiveness.
approach: Analyzes how action-chunking and exploratory augmentation circumvent exponential error compounding through control-theoretic stability as key mechanism.
contribution: Provides tighter theoretical guarantees on IL error and validates control-theoretic insights through robot learning benchmarks.

problem: Reconstructing closed surface meshes from noisy point clouds with guaranteed simply connected topology is challenging.
approach: Combines Delaunay triangulation with robust volumetric mesh reconstruction ensuring simply connected topology, using spectral initial orientations and iterative reorientation.
contribution: Guarantees topological correctness while reconstructing mesh approximating input triangles on real and synthetic datasets.

problem: Building promptable behavioral foundation models for real-world humanoid control that enable zero-shot and few-shot adaptation on diverse downstream tasks remains largely unexplored.
approach: BFM-Zero learns shared latent representation embedding motions, goals, and rewards via unsupervised RL and FB models, enabling versatile inference through motion tracking, goal reaching, and reward inference.
contribution: Demonstrates zero-shot motion tracking, goal reaching, reward inference, and few-shot adaptation on Unitree G1 humanoid in real world.

problem: Existing LLM benchmarks fail to differentiate question difficulty, limiting their ability to effectively distinguish model capabilities.
approach: RankLLM introduces difficulty as primary criterion via bidirectional score propagation between models and questions, enabling difficulty-aware evaluation.
contribution: Achieves 90% agreement with human judgments on 30 models and 35,550 questions, demonstrating stability, fast convergence, and computational efficiency.

problem: Deep RL-based NFV resource allocation research lacks systematic benchmark for comprehensive simulation and rigorous evaluation, hindering algorithm development.
approach: Virne provides customizable simulations for diverse network scenarios, integrates over 30 methods, and establishes rigorous evaluation protocol extending beyond online effectiveness.
contribution: Enables comprehensive analysis through diverse simulations, rich implementations, and thorough evaluation providing insights into performance tradeoffs.

problem: Current 3D object editing approaches are inefficient, inconsistent, and fail to preserve unedited regions; most methods introduce artifacts through multi-view reconstruction.
approach: Nano3D integrates FlowEdit into TRELLIS with region-aware merging strategies (Voxel/Slat-Merge) ensuring consistency between edited and unedited areas.
contribution: Achieves superior 3D consistency and visual quality; introduces Nano3D-Edit-100k, the first large-scale 3D editing dataset with over 100,000 high-quality pairs.

problem: Whether decoder-based CLM-pretrained models truly outperform encoder-based MLM-pretrained models on text representation tasks remains unclear when controlling for confounds like scale and data.
approach: Conducts large-scale controlled pretraining ablations training 38 models (210M-1B parameters) and 15,000+ fine-tuning runs comparing MLM and CLM strategies.
contribution: Shows MLM generally yields better text representation performance and CLM is more data-efficient; biphasic CLM-then-MLM achieves optimal performance under fixed budget.

problem: Large language models' computational costs limit practical application despite reasoning capabilities; the inefficiency stems from tight coupling of cognitive planning and linguistic realization.
approach: Proposes latent guidance decoupling: large model as Implicit Thinker performs planning and compresses strategy into latent vectors; small model as Explicit Executor uses guidance for reasoning chains.
contribution: Boosts small model accuracy by up to 13.9%, achieves 2x speedup over baseline, and up to 4x faster than large model while substantially enhancing reasoning across 8 benchmarks.
